Safe setup: Synthetic customer and order in a non-production environment
Recovery source and point: Select a restore point before the test deletion; preserve the current snapshot
Isolated target: New database branch or project; never overwrite the only source
Database and files: Restore the record and verify referenced files separately
Application and configuration: Deploy the compatible application version and migration state
Identity and access: Test customer and staff roles separately
External systems: No live emails, payments or webhooks
Validation evidence: Record ID, row checks, file open test, workflow recording

Failure scenario: Bad schema migration or corrupt write
Safe setup: Apply a reversible test migration to synthetic data
Recovery source and point: Choose the last known-good database point before the migration
Database and files: Check tables, indexes, constraints, sequences and representative records
Application and configuration: Pin the application version compatible with the restored schema
Identity and access: Verify role grants and least-privilege access
External systems: Keep scheduled jobs and outbound integrations disabled
Validation evidence: Migration history, schema diff, sample queries and critical workflow

Failure scenario: Lost uploaded files or object storage
Safe setup: Delete a synthetic test object from a test bucket only
Recovery source and point: Use the independent object backup or documented storage export
Isolated target: Separate bucket or project with private access
Database and files: Restore object bytes and compare hashes; verify database metadata points to them
Application and configuration: Confirm application file URLs and upload/download paths
Identity and access: Check signed URL and access policy behaviour
Validation evidence: Object count, checksums, access tests and sample download

Safe setup: Deploy a known-bad build to a protected preview or test environment
Recovery source and point: Select the last known-good deployment and record the commit
Database and files: Confirm database state is compatible; do not assume rollback restores data
Application and configuration: Rollback code and separately verify environment variables, runtime settings and cron definitions
Identity and access: Test sign-in and permissions against the current identity provider
External systems: Check external APIs and database state independently
Validation evidence: Deployment ID, config checklist, health check and customer workflow

Safe setup: Use a disposable test credential; never copy production secrets into the worksheet
Recovery source and point: Use the documented secret inventory and approved rotation process
Isolated target: Isolated environment with newly issued test credentials
Database and files: Confirm database connection and encrypted data access
Application and configuration: Recreate required environment variables without exposing values
Identity and access: Verify auth keys, service roles and session behaviour
External systems: Rotate provider tokens and webhook secrets in test mode
Validation evidence: Secret inventory version, successful connection and rejected old credential

Safe setup: Use synthetic users and a test identity provider
Recovery source and point: Restore user records only where supported; separately export required configuration
Isolated target: Isolated auth project or test tenant
Database and files: Verify user records, identities and role mappings
Application and configuration: Restore callback URLs, allowed origins and auth configuration
Identity and access: Test sign-in, sign-out, MFA, password reset and staff permissions
External systems: Disable production email/SMS delivery during the drill
Validation evidence: Synthetic account results, permission matrix and auth logs

Failure scenario: Payment event arrived after the restore point
Safe setup: Use provider test mode and synthetic transaction references
Recovery source and point: Restore app records to a point before a known test payment event
Database and files: Compare internal order and payment references with provider test records
Application and configuration: Run server-side transaction verification before changing order state
Identity and access: Use test credentials and restrict staff access
External systems: Check payment status, refund and settlement references; never charge a live customer
Validation evidence: Provider reference, verified status, internal order state and reconciliation exception

Failure scenario: Duplicate scheduled job or webhook after restore
Safe setup: Use a test queue and synthetic event; block production egress
Recovery source and point: Restore a database snapshot that contains pending work
Database and files: Check outbox, event IDs, idempotency keys and processing state
Application and configuration: Keep workers paused until the test owner authorises execution
Identity and access: Use test secrets and synthetic recipients
External systems: Prevent duplicate payment, refund, email, SMS or delivery effects
Validation evidence: Before/after event counts, idempotency result and outbound request log

Safe setup: Simulate timeout or unavailable API in a test environment
Recovery source and point: Restore the latest internally consistent state; external provider remains authoritative for its own records
Isolated target: Isolated service with controlled network access
Database and files: Confirm pending work is durable and retryable
Application and configuration: Verify timeout, backoff, circuit-breaker and manual exception paths
Identity and access: Keep service credentials valid but test-only
External systems: Reconcile provider state before replaying operations
Validation evidence: Queue depth, retry log, provider reference and final state

Safe setup: Use a test subdomain or local routing override
Recovery source and point: Use current deployment and documented DNS/certificate records
Isolated target: Staging hostname with no customer traffic
Database and files: Confirm database is unchanged and reachable from the target runtime
Application and configuration: Verify deployment alias, DNS records, TLS certificate and redirect behaviour
Identity and access: Test login callbacks and allowed origins
External systems: Check webhook endpoints and partner allowlists
Validation evidence: DNS lookup, TLS result, route check and login workflow

Failure scenario: Provider project or account becomes unavailable
Safe setup: Use an independent export and a separate recovery account/project
Recovery source and point: Choose an off-provider copy and record its age and integrity
Isolated target: New project in a controlled region with cost approval before any paid restore
Database and files: Restore database and separately restore storage objects
Application and configuration: Recreate functions, integrations, environment variables and scheduled jobs
Identity and access: Reconfigure auth, API keys, roles and permissions
External systems: Reconnect payment, email, messaging and delivery providers in test mode
Validation evidence: Restore log, dependency checklist, sample queries and end-to-end test

Failure scenario: Full business recovery and customer return
Safe setup: Run a scheduled exercise with synthetic users and a written rollback boundary
Recovery source and point: Use a named backup and a documented recovery timestamp
Isolated target: Isolated recovery environment, then a separately approved cutover rehearsal
Database and files: Validate records, files, permissions and data integrity
Application and configuration: Deploy the selected code and reconstruct configuration
Identity and access: Prove customer and staff access with least privilege
External systems: Reconcile payments, refunds, settlements, inventory, delivery and communications
Validation evidence: Timeline, workflow evidence, exception register, customer update and sign-off
